body.estimand_functional: \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI}}=I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}\) when \(s=1\); when \(1<s\le2\), it is the full-parameter fallback if \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{prof}}=1\) or a displayed deterministic/denominator check fails, and otherwise it is \(\operatorname{hull}\{\theta\in\Theta:|\widehat y-\theta\widehat d|\le2r_{\mathrm{prof}}\}\) at the returned center \(\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}\).

sampling_model.design: Independent random design with \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and a law-specific unknown cutoff \(c_P\in[1/4,3/4]\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument is \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge c_P\}\), and monotone response types imply \(D_i=D_i(Z_i)\).
sampling_model.outcome: Binary potential outcomes obey consistency \(Y_i=Y_i(D_i)\); exclusion is encoded by the absence of a direct \(Z_i\) argument.
sampling_model.overlap: Uniformly on both sides of the cutoff, \(\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X=x,\ell)\ge v\) and the absolute conditional outcome--treatment correlation is at most \(1-v\); when the conditional treatment variance is zero, covariance is zero and the correlation inequality is interpreted directly without forming a correlation coefficient.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: One-sided observable treatment and outcome regressions admit radius-\(M\), order-\(s\) H\"older extensions.  The proved \(s=1\) procedure uses deterministic four-fold splitting, fixed-denominator boundary-kernel treatment contrasts, a coarse \(H/64\)-resolution scan, an independent local mesh refinement, and fixed-center transformed-outcome inversion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their bias-aware Anderson--Rubin inversion delivers honest weak-first-stage inference when the cutoff is known.
Their unknown-cutoff analysis obtains oracle substitution under a fixed discontinuity in a sharp-design treatment-effect problem.
Their ordered-modulus construction optimizes fixed-level expected length on convex fixed-index regression classes.
The paper studies nonparametric location estimation with a shrinking discontinuity under smoothness restrictions.
Their multiscale work supplies scan architecture and exponential change-point control for step-function signals.
Their Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap theory provides general maximal-control tools for suprema of empirical processes.
Their Bayesian model propagates unknown-cutoff posterior uncertainty into fuzzy-RD effect estimation.
Their working paper treats fuzzy regression discontinuity and unknown-discontinuity estimation in separate extensions.

body.tldr: The paper studies fixed-\(\alpha\) expected length of connected honest intervals for fuzzy-RD LATE when both the compliance jump and its unknown cutoff become statistically weak.  The finite-sample location-mixture converse proves a nonshrinking barrier below the signal-to-entropy boundary.  At \(s=1\), a total four-fold rectangular scan--refine--invert rule attains the known-cutoff order when \(n\kappa_n^3\) dominates \(\log(e/\kappa_n)\).  For \(s>1\), an explicit affine-profile map and fallback are defined, but the same-class bracket \(\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\}\) remains an open question because its profile maximal inequality and matching slope-kink lower pair are not yet proved.  The fixed-level critical-window law also remains open.

project_justification.gap: Known-cutoff weak fuzzy-RD inference and fixed-jump unknown-cutoff localization do not characterize honest connected LATE-interval length when the first-stage denominator and its location weaken jointly; in particular, neither supplies the higher-smoothness cutoff-uncertainty term under separate one-sided smoothness.
project_justification.niche: The joint experiment combines a nonconvex union over cutoff locations, a causal outcome--treatment ratio, separate one-sided smoothness that permits a derivative kink, and fixed-level connected-length loss.  Its critical and higher-smoothness detectable regions cannot be inferred from a point-estimation cutoff rate.
project_justification.fill: The project fixes one observable-law class, proves the finite-sample location-mixture converse, and gives a total four-fold interval attaining known-cutoff order on the Lipschitz face.  For \(s>1\), it now exposes a measurable common-versus-piecewise affine profile with an explicit fallback and isolates the unresolved bracket \(\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\}\) without strengthening the class or claiming unproved constants.

body.related_work: Noack and Rothe (2024) motivate the observable class and known-cutoff bias-aware Anderson--Rubin inversion for weak fuzzy-RD designs.  Porter and Yu (2015) obtain unknown-cutoff oracle substitution under a fixed discontinuity in a sharp-design treatment-effect problem.  Frick, Munk, and Sieling (2014) motivate multiscale scan architecture, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014) provide general maximal-control tools; neither supplies the present uniform causal connected-length theorem.  M{\"u}ller and Song (1997) and Tuvaandorj (2020) concern shrinking-jump or nonparametric location experiments, and no equation-level proposition from Tuvaandorj is used here.  Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018) supply an ordered-modulus and test-inversion template for convex fixed-index classes.  Madrid Padilla, Yu, Wang, and Rinaldo (2022) study aligned multivariate change channels without the monotone fuzzy-RD causal restrictions.  Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version) use a Bayesian unknown-cutoff fuzzy-RD model, and Arai, Otsu, and Seo (2026) discuss fuzzy and unknown-discontinuity extensions separately.  The proved frontier advance here consists of the finite-sample converse and the Lipschitz oracle-attainment theorem.  The higher-smoothness bracket and the exact critical-window connected-length law remain explicit open questions.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The higher-smoothness profile branch is a total measurable estimator, not a proved performance theorem.  Its unit-flank population Gram has exact minimum eigenvalue \(H(4-\sqrt{13})/6\), its fallback uses half that value, and the approximation tolerance is \(\delta=\kappa_n/32\).  The stopped Bernstein inequality is derived, but the uniform population-to-empirical comparison for the quadratic profile has not been closed, so the previously suggested \(2^{-28}\) and \(2^{-30}\) constants are not asserted.  A same-class slope-kink converse for \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) and the sharp critical-window law also remain open.
body.honest_scope: The Wald interpretation, known-cutoff benchmark, and finite-sample location-mixture barrier retain their full stated scope.  Oracle-order attainment is proved only on the Lipschitz face \(s=1\), uniformly over vanishing \(\kappa_n\) satisfying the displayed signal condition.  For \(s>1\), the paper defines the profile-based rule and poses, but does not claim, the detectable-region bracket.  No cross-side derivative matching, latent-cell H{\"o}lder restriction, adaptation guarantee, disconnected-set result, or matched critical-window constant is added.
body.interpretation: At \(s=1\), the localization index \(n\kappa_n^3\) pays the logarithmic search cost, after which an independent fixed-center inversion has length \(n^{-1/3}/\kappa_n\), exactly the known-cutoff order.  For \(s>1\), separate affine profiling is designed to absorb an unrestricted derivative kink.  If it localizes at order \(1/(n\kappa_n^2)\), the kink contributes \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) after division by the compliance jump; proving that localization and a matching lower pair is the remaining detectable-region problem.
